story_review.one_viewing_summary: A driverless car picks up at a San Antonio airport curb with nobody at the wheel. Service started in a limited 60 square mile area in February. In April two empty cars ended up in floodwater, one carried down a creek and one stranded on a street, each disclosed as a different illustrated case. A federal software recall covering 3,791 cars says the software may let a car slow, then drive into standing water. The record lists the remedy as under development. As an interim step the weather limits were tightened and every car was updated by April 20. The ride stays open while the remedy is unfinished.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The film opens on the airport ride ('can anyone ride?') and ends on the same curb with the door open, beside the remedy row marked under development. The ending answers what the record says without inventing a fix or an outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: s1 to s2 at 6.8/7.0 s: a cut from the phone at the curb to a blank tabletop map. The board's 'car pin rides onto the map' bridge appears only as a few-pixel mark at 12.0 to 12.8 s.
